text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of "Do Not Destroy." A miktam of David, when he fled from Saul into the cave.
Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me, for in you my soul takes refuge. In the shadow of your wings I will take refuge until the destroying storms pass by.
I call to God Most High, to God who fulfills his purpose for me.
He sends from heaven and saves me; he rebukes the one who tramples me. Selah. God sends out his steadfast love and his faithfulness.
My soul lies down among lions; I lie among those who breathe out fire, men whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are a sharp sword.

versions.text: My soul lies down among lions; I lie among those who breathe out fire, men whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharpened swords.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has the singular 'a sharp sword' (חֶרֶב חַדָּה); the singular image is more vivid and matches the text. Also 'sharpened' slightly overtranslates חַדָּה ('sharp').

text: Be exalted above the heavens, O God; let your glory be over all the earth.
They spread a net for my feet; my soul was bowed down. They dug a pit before me, but they have fallen into it themselves. Selah.
My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast; I will sing and make music.
Awake, my glory! Awake, harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn.
I will praise you among the peoples, O Lord; I will sing your praise among the nations.

versions.text: I will praise you among the peoples, O Lord; I will sing of you among the nations.
versions.explanation: The verb אֲזַמֶּרְךָ carries a direct object suffix ('I will sing praises to you'), which is stronger than the vaguer 'sing of you.' The suggested wording keeps the parallel with the first line and reads well aloud.

text: For your steadfast love is great to the heavens, your faithfulness to the clouds.
Be exalted above the heavens, O God; let your glory be over all the earth.
